Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) restored its Microsoft 365 services Friday after a nearly 24-hour global outage blocked access to Outlook mailboxes and disrupted parts of Teams and Copilot.
GuruFocus has detected 5 Warning Sign with MSFT.
Features in Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 apps that rely on Exchange Online also experienced problems, though much of that software remained accessible.
At the worst point, more than 80% of the servers in the affected gateway fleet were unresponsive.
It said customers were no longer experiencing active disruptions by 11:10 a.m.
Investors Takeaway  Microsoft's final incident report, expected Nov. 20, should detail what the company plans to change so a failure in one region stays contained.
The business question is whether customers change how they buy or use Microsoft 365 after the outage.

Cision    View original content to download multimedia:https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/thread-ai-joins-the-microsoft-for-startups-pegasus-program-to-deliver-its-ai-workflow-orchestration-platform-on-microsoft-marketplace-302940646.html       Many investors own S&P 500 index funds because they view them as a diversified investment.
In one sense, it's true, since you'll have exposure to about 500 companies.
However, the S&P 500 index is weighted by market cap, so the largest companies have the most influence.
And thanks to the rise of trillion-dollar technology companies, the top players are bigger than ever.
In fact, the 10 largest stocks now make up nearly 40% of the index.
Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) alone accounts for about 7.5%.
Missed AI's "Act 1"?
Act 2 Could Be 16x Bigger.
Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005.
But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase.
"Act 2" is the global rollout.
Continue »  There is, however, an alternative that allows you to invest in the S&P 500 with less concentration in the market's largest companies.

How equal weighting works  An equal-weight fund, such as the Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF (NYSEMKT:RSP), owns the same companies as any S&P 500 ETF you may own, but it gives each one about 0.2% of the portfolio and rebalances every quarter to bring them back to equal.
As a result, technology stocks accounted for about 17% of the fund as of late August, compared with about 38% in the standard S&P 500.
It's also cheaper on a valuation basis, at about 16.7 times forward earnings versus about 19.7 for the cap-weighted index.
Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF charges a 0.20% expense ratio, compared with just 0.03% for the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (NYSEMKT:VOO).
In 2022, when large tech stocks fell sharply after the pandemic-era surge, Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF lost about 11.6%, compared with about 18.2% for the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY).
In 2008, Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF lost about 40%, compared with about 37% for SPY, and its peak-to-trough decline was deeper than that of the cap-weighted fund.
Since its launch in 2003, Invesco S&P 500 Equal Weight ETF has returned about 11.2% per year, versus about 11.5% for SPY.
Equal weight lagged badly from 2023 through 2025 as the largest tech stocks surged, although it was slightly ahead so far in 2026 as of late October.
The bottom line  An equal-weight S&P 500 fund diversifies you away from big tech, but it won't protect you in every downturn.
If you're uncomfortable with how much of your portfolio rides on a handful of stocks, putting a portion of your S&P 500 allocation in an equal-weight fund is a reasonable compromise.

However, if you already have a substantial amount of mega-cap tech exposure in your portfolio, it could be a solid alternative to traditional S&P 500 ETFs that will add significantly more exposure to the stocks you already own.

The global joint all-domain command and control (JADC2) systems market is experiencing strong growth as governments and defense organizations invest in connected, data-driven military operations.
The market is projected to increase from $43.55 billion in 2025 to $45.98 billion in 2026, representing a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 5.6%.

Expanding defense modernization programs, increased deployment of satellites and battlefield sensors, digitization of military communications, and the need for greater interoperability among allied forces have also accelerated demand for JADC2 systems.
The JADC2 systems market is forecast to reach $57.69 billion by 2030, expanding at a CAGR of 5.8% from 2026.

Key JADC2 market trends include the use of AI-enabled multi-domain data fusion to improve real-time battlefield awareness and the development of interoperable command architectures connecting multiple defense branches.

JADC2 platforms support these objectives by combining AI-enabled data fusion, secure communications, advanced sensors, and interoperable networks to enable faster decisions across air, land, sea, space, and cyber operations.
Story Continues       In the United States, the Department of Defense's fiscal year 2024 Cybersecurity and Acquisition budget totaled $13.5 billion.

The funding was aligned with priorities established under the 2022 National Defense Strategy and supported continued progress under the Digital Modernization Strategy and Department of Defense Cyber Strategy.

Technology providers are also investing in software-based JADC2 capabilities that enable real-time data integration, secure multi-domain connectivity, and AI-supported decision-making across distributed defense networks.

In March 2025, Lockheed Martin introduced its CJADC2 Interoperability Factory, a self-funded software capability designed to connect advanced warfighting systems and support the Department of Defense's Combined Joint All-Domain Command and Control vision.
Strategic partnerships are further supporting innovation in the JADC2 systems market.
In December 2025, Lockheed Martin partnered with XTEND to enhance situational awareness capabilities through autonomous systems, artificial intelligence, and edge computing.
North America was the dominant region in the joint all-domain command and control systems market in 2025, supported by substantial defense technology investment and ongoing military modernization.

Palantir Technologies PLTR raised its 2026 outlook after another earnings beat and a sharp acceleration in AI-driven demand.
The Nov. 2 update showed commercial adoption broadening while profitability and cash generation remained elevated.
PLTR's Q3 Beat Shows AI Demand Staying Strong  Palantir reported third-quarter earnings of 44 cents per share, 7.3% above the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 41 cents.
Revenues of roughly $2.3 billion beat the consensus mark by 6.5%, increased 96% year over year and rose 20% sequentially.
NVIDIA Corporation NVDA reported fiscal second-quarter 2027 Data Center revenue of $89 billion, up 117% year over year, reflecting continued AI infrastructure demand.
Microsoft Corporation MSFT reported 19% revenue growth in its fiscal first quarter of 2027 and said customers are seeking greater capability, choice and cost efficiency across its technology stack.
Palantir Raises Its 2026 Revenue Outlook  Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $8.530-$8.534 billion from the prior $8.150-$8.158 billion range.
For the fourth quarter, Palantir expects revenues of $2.649-$2.653 billion, which would extend sequential growth from the third quarter.
Full-year U.S. commercial revenues are now expected to exceed $3.559 billion, representing growth of at least 143%.
U.S. commercial revenues reached $984 million, up 148% year over year, while U.S. government revenues were $953 million, up 96%.

U.S. commercial customer count increased to 686 from 530 a year earlier, while companywide net dollar retention climbed to 165% from 157% in the second quarter, showing that existing customers increased spending.
Palantir's Margin Gains Face Higher Investment  Adjusted operating margin reached 62% in the third quarter, up from 51% a year earlier.
Operating cash flow totaled $1.205 billion, equal to a 52% margin, giving Palantir substantial internally generated resources to support continued development and deployment.
Adjusted expenses increased 20% sequentially and 53% year over year to $887 million, driven by investment in AIP and technical hiring.
Over the past 60 days, earnings estimates for 2026 and 2027 have moved 5.6% and 10.2% higher, respectively, reinforcing the strength of the current growth trend.
